articles.summary: Avionics system updates help ensure mission readiness for CH-47 fleetHUNTSVILLE, Ala., Aug. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The U.S. Army awarded Collins Aerospace, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, a contract worth up to $472 million to provide engineering services that support the modernization and sustainment of the CH‑47 Chinook fleet.The engineering services will deliver avionics upgrades that help integrate new capabilities more efficiently, address obsolescence and strengthen the aircraft's avionics architecture to support continued mission readiness in a rapidly evolving operational environment.
articles.title: RTX's Collins Aerospace to support modernization of U.S. Army's Chinook helicopters

articles.summary: Expansion toboost production capacity for critical defense systems and create 100 high-skill jobs FOREST, Miss., Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has completed a 17,000 square-foot expansion of its Forest, Mississippi manufacturing facility. Supported by a $50 million capital investment, the project will boost production capacity for critical electronic warfare and radar systems and is expected to create 100 high-skill jobs by 2028.
articles.title: RTX's Raytheon completes $50 million expansion of Mississippi manufacturing facility

articles.summary: Output has jumped 20% each year since 2024 and production time has dropped by the same margin at Pratt & Whitney AutoAir in Holt, Michigan. That facility is one of several where RTX is demonstrating digital technologies as part of a broader data strategy to connect the company’s systems, factories and products to speed production, reduce costs, improve quality and equip products with powerful new capabilities. At the site level, the effects are clear. “We’re seeing record numbers of blades going out the doors,” said Bryce Bergethon, the Holt site’s operations excellence manager. Here’s how it works. Tracking parts in real time One of the main capabilities the site uses is called Real-Time Location Services, or RTLS – a “needle-in-a-haystack” system that can find any of the thousands of parts flowing through the factory at any given time. When a small batch of parts had been sent across the factory for rework and never returned, for example, a supervisor used the system to test his best guess on where they were. He was right. The parts had piled up at a workstation, awaiting a treatment that had been taking up to several hours. With the mystery solved, the team used the insight to speed up the step in question, eventually finding a faster alternative that worked as well in only a fraction of the time.
articles.title: A production boost, powered by hard data

articles.summary: First‑of‑its‑kind demo advances autonomous undersea operationsPORTSMOUTH, R.I., Aug. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, and Composite Energy Technologies (CET) have successfully demonstrated the undersea launch capabilities of HADALUS, a new, low-cost, long-endurance unmanned undersea vehicle (UUV).During a recent U.S. Navy exercise, the UUV completed a series of at-sea missions on a Navy undersea test range, successfully demonstrating its undersea launch capabilities while submerged. This marks the first time the U.S. Navy has seen this integrated capability in the water and points toward a future where a single unmanned undersea platform can perform detect, reacquire and engage functions within one mission.
articles.title: RTX's Raytheon and Composite Energy Technology successfully demonstrate new unmanned undersea vehicle

articles.summary: WALLOPS ISLAND, Va., Aug. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has delivered and installed the first SPY-6(V)4 radar array at Surface Combat Systems Center at Wallops Island in Virginia, marking a major milestone for the U.S. Navy's Flight IIA Destroyer modernization effort and the SPY-6 backfit program. The Wallops site, a land‑based test facility situated over an open-water environment, will support extensive testing of the radar and its power and combat system interfaces ahead of installation on USS Pinckney (DDG 91), the first ship to be backfit with SPY‑6(V)4.SPY-6(V)4 is one of four variants in the SPY-6 family of radars, and is the only variant designed to backfit Flight IIA Destroyers. Initial testing will begin later this year and continue through mid‑2028.
articles.title: RTX's Raytheon completes installation of first SPY-6(V)4 array at Wallops Island test site

articles.summary: Contract accelerates production of critical precision-strike weaponTUCSON, Ariz., Aug. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, will dramatically accelerate the production of Tomahawk cruise missiles for the U.S. Navy over the multi-year period under the terms of an unprecedented $22.9 billion contract, awarded as part of the Department of War's Arsenal of Freedom.This contract follows the landmark agreements between Raytheon and the Department of War and supports the annual production ramp to more than 1,000 Tomahawk missiles and associated support, ensuring a stable, predictable supply for the Navy and allies.
